title: What Does <T> Mean?
instructions: What does `<T>` mean in the class declaration `class Box<T>`?

options.text: T is a variable that stores the text inside the box
T is a placeholder for any type, decided when you create an instance
T means the class can only hold String values
T is a special Kotlin keyword for testing

explanation: The `<T>` in `class Box<T>` declares a type parameter. `T` is a placeholder that gets replaced with a real type (like `Int`, `String`, or `Double`) when you create an instance. For example, `Box<Int>(42)` replaces `T` with `Int`. This lets one class work with many different types.
